raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The clinical presentation of mental retardation, seizures, and facial angiofibromas (Pringle fibro-adenomas) is classic for Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. Pulmonary involvement in this condition typically manifests as lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM), which presents radiographically as a diffuse reticular or reticulonodular pattern due to cystic lung disease, matching the findings in the provided chest X-ray.
